question: The forks on my pallet truck are bent. What do I do, who needs to know, and what do I put in the log?
note: Changed on 2026-11-13. The old question ('What do I do and who needs to know?') could be fully answered from SOP-EQ-01 alone: s4 and s5 cover the steps, logging the same shift, and escalation to the Senior FLM. So citing SOP-IR-01 was optional, and a correct answer that cited only SOP-EQ-01 failed. Asking what goes in the log makes SOP-IR-01 genuinely required, because only SOP-IR-01 s1.3 says what to record.
key_facts: Stop using it straight away and do not work around the fault
Park it safely: forks fully lowered, out of aisles, clear of fire exits
Attach a 'Do Not Use — Faulty' tag with the fault, date and who found it
Never repair it yourself; maintenance does repairs
Tell the FLM straight away and log it the same shift
The log records what happened, where, when, who was involved and any immediate action taken (SOP-IR-01 s1.3)
The FLM reports to maintenance and escalates to the Senior FLM the same shift

question: I'm an FLM. We keep getting damaged pallets and damaged goods from the same supplier. What should happen?

Individual incidents are still logged, recording the supplier for pallets that arrived with a delivery

question: A pallet of liquid chemicals has leaked across the aisle.
note: Coverage accepts 'partial' or 'full'. SOP-IR-01 fully covers the operative's part (make the area safe, notify the FLM, who tells the Shift Manager, then log it), and s3.2 leaves resolving the hazard to the FLM. It gives no clean-up method, so 'partial' is also correct. Either way the judge still fails any invented clean-up method (last key fact).
key_facts: Make the area safe first: cordon off the spill and clear people
Notify the FLM immediately
The FLM informs the Shift Manager straight away for a chemical spill
Log the incident
No spill clean-up method is in the SOPs, so none should be invented
